record.original_question: For the same discretized sparse crystallography problem, which reconstruction methods can recover the unknown weights and locations efficiently and stably, and under what assumptions on the probe and on the set of probe shifts do those methods work?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7. What methods can be used to solve this problem efficiently and stably, and under what conditions on the probe w and the set of the probe shifts R?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $n \geq 1$ and $N \geq 1$. Consider signals on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ of the form
$$ f = \mathbf{1} + \sum_{j=1}^{N} a_j\, e_{t_j}, $$
where $\mathbf{1}$ is the all-ones vector (the background), $e_t \in \mathbb{C}^n$ denotes the standard basis vector supported at position $t \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, the unknown atom locations $t_1,\dots,t_N \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ are distinct, and $a_1,\dots,a_N \in \mathbb{C}$ are unknown weights.

Fix a probe vector $w \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and a finite set of probe shifts $R \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. For $r \in R$, let $S_r$ denote the cyclic shift operator defined by $(S_r w)_t = w_{t-r}$, and let $F$ denote the discrete Fourier transform on $\mathbb{C}^n$. The measurements are the squared magnitudes
$$ y_{r,k} \;=\; \left| (Fw)_k + \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{j=1}^{N} a_j\, (S_r w)_{t_j}\, e^{-2\pi i k(t_j - r)/n} \right|^2, \qquad r \in R,\; k \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}. $$

Determine reconstruction algorithms that recover the unknown weights $\{a_j\}$ and locations $\{t_j\}$ from the measurements $\{y_{r,k}\}$ both efficiently (in polynomial time in $n$ and $N$) and stably (with provable noise robustness), and identify sufficient conditions on the probe $w$ and on the shift set $R$ under which such algorithms succeed.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a 2025 survey of selected open problems in phase retrieval; no published efficient and stable reconstruction algorithm with explicit conditions on the probe and shift set has been identified for this discretized sparse crystallography model.

status_evidence.title: Phasebook: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: Section 4.2 presents sparse crystallography with probe w and shifts R, asking what methods solve the problem efficiently and stably and under what conditions on w and R.
status_evidence.claim: The reconstruction question is explicitly listed as an open problem.
